text: Where is the retry limit defined in this repo? npm test is failing against a flaky upstream; run it, figure out why, raise the limit to 5 using a shell command, and rerun npm test to confirm.
{"command":"cat package.json && ls -R lib && git status --short","description":"Inspect package.json, lib directory, and git status"}
{"command":"cat lib/retry.js && echo ---- && cat retry.test.js && echo ---- && npm test; echo \"exit=$?\"","description":"Show retry code and tests, then run npm test"}

{"command":"sed -i '' 's/^export const MAX_RETRIES = 3;/export const MAX_RETRIES = 5;/' lib/retry.js && head -1 lib/retry.js && npm test; echo \"exit=$?\"","description":"Raise MAX_RETRIES to 5 and rerun npm test"}

export const MAX_RETRIES = 5;

> fetcher@1.0.0 test
> node retry.test.js

retry tests passed after 5 calls
exit=0

The retry limit is defined as `MAX_RETRIES` in `lib/retry.js:1`. I raised it from 3 to 5, and `npm test` now passes.

**Why it was failing:** This wasn't flakiness. `retry.test.js` makes the mocked upstream throw on the first 4 calls and expects the 5th to succeed. `withRetry` only makes `MAX_RETRIES` attempts, so with a limit of 3 it gave up after the third call and rethrew `flaky upstream`.

**Change:** `sed` changed `export const MAX_RETRIES = 3;` to `= 5;` in `lib/retry.js`. No other code changed.

**Verification:** After the change, `npm test` exited 0 with `retry tests passed after 5 calls`.

The repo also contains an untracked `.memory/` directory with a session log that includes your request. I didn't change or use it.
